accepted_judgments: Both reports answer finite decision-support questions, are within their requested report budgets, use named immutable upstream revisions and contain no patches or implementation claims.
R929's exact SGLang model order and separate HC/PLE/GDN state semantics are useful; the vLLM GDN discussion is a related-model analogy at the cited old revision.
R930's device-side route metadata proposal is a defensible measured-dependency experiment, not a claim that the 52.433-second interval is removable routing work.

FP32 local accumulation, reductions and recurrent state remain distinct from tensor storage. Cross-chunk state, PLE history ordering, layer callback publication, route-slot mapping, bounds, faults and physical 262,144-context gates remain required.

No report establishes a greater-than-600 tok/s result, clean speed gain, production numerical qualification, model-quality acceptance, or inference adoption. The prior clean 403.0 tok/s median remains separate from the instrumented run.

corrections.correction: Interpret exact BF16 residual bits as a required control for preserving the BF16 store boundary in the same-operation fusion experiment. Exact FP32 scale equality is a useful same-order equivalence check only when the same reduction ordering is retained. If fusion changes the reduction tree, compare storage, FP32 accumulation/reduction, normalization constant, and rounding locations against the validated SGLang/vLLM production contract; do not impose the old extra-precision FP32 output or exact-internal-scale result as a general adoption criterion. Apply the same production-contract rule to the HC-mix reuse candidate's parity/quality gate.
corrections.evidence: AGENTS.md's 2026-10-16 numerical-reference policy; SGLang GroupedGemmaRMSNorm returns the input dtype after FP32 normalization arithmetic, and Qwen4-Exp only reuses prepared norms when no PLE or row movement intervenes. The report's exact comparisons remain useful diagnostic controls, not the universal acceptance policy.
